The verifiable-by-hand numbers marked in the keys.

recall.question: What is the topic of lesson 07?
recall.answer: Trees and ensembles.

recall.question: How were the numbers produced?
recall.answer: All numbers were computed 2026-10-06 unless marked as hand arithmetic.

keyTerms.definition: The axis-aligned regions the tree votes on.
The leaf label assigned to each rectangle.

recall.question: What are the three rectangles?
recall.answer: x1 at most 0.5 votes 0, x1 above 0.5 with x2 at most 0.5 votes 1, and both above 0.5 votes 1.

keyTerms.definition: The leaf vote for a point, here 1 and 0.
The first split feature with threshold 0.5.

keyTerms.definition: The impurity 1 minus the sum of squared class shares, here 0.18.
The log impurity, here 0.3251.

recall.question: What are the three impurity values for p = [0.9, 0.1]?
recall.answer: Gini is 0.18, entropy is 0.3251, and misclassification is 0.1.

keyTerms.definition: The impurity at its max of 0.5 for balanced classes.
The log impurity at ln 2 = 0.6931.

recall.question: What are the impurity values for balanced classes?
recall.answer: Gini is 0.5, entropy is 0.6931, and misclassification is 0.5.

keyTerms.definition: The split impurity computed per child.
The size-weighted average of child impurities, here 0.25.

recall.question: What is the weighted child Gini at t = 0.7?
recall.answer: It is 0.25: the left child has Gini 0.375 on 4 of 6 points and the right is pure.

keyTerms.definition: Parent impurity minus weighted child impurity, here 0.5.
Children with Gini 0, so the split explains all impurity.

recall.question: What is the gain when both children are pure?
recall.answer: It is 0.5, equal to the parent Gini.

keyTerms.definition: The split improvement, here 0 for both Gini and entropy.
The impurity stuck at 0.5 in both children.

recall.question: What is the greedy stall?
recall.answer: All single-split gains are 0 for both Gini and entropy.

keyTerms.definition: The depth-1 tree splitting at t = 0.475.
The single error: x = 0.7 with label 0 called 1.
The training error 1/8 = 0.125.

recall.question: What is the stump error?
recall.answer: It is 0.125: the point x = 0.7 with label 0 falls right and is called 1, the single miss.

recall.question: What does the stump predict?
recall.answer: It predicts 0 left and 1 right of t = 0.475.

keyTerms.definition: The complexity price 0.2 per leaf.
Error plus alpha times leaves: 0.525 versus 0.8.

recall.question: Which depth does alpha 0.2 pick?
recall.answer: Depth 1: its cost 0.525 beats the depth-2 cost 0.8.

keyTerms.definition: The 1000^1000 possible bootstrap draws at n = 1000.
The method, since enumeration is hopeless.

recall.question: Why is sampling the method?
recall.answer: There are 1000^1000 possible replicates, so enumeration is hopeless.

keyTerms.definition: The probability equal to 81/256 = 0.3164.
The computed value of the probability.

recall.question: What is (3/4)^4?

keyTerms.definition: The bagged average variance decomposed into single and pair terms.
The pairwise correlation between trees.
What rho measures across the B trees.

recall.question: What is the bagging variance formula?
recall.answer: It is rho sigma squared plus (1 - rho) sigma squared over B.

recall.question: What dominates at large B?
recall.answer: The rho sigma squared term: the shared wobble.

keyTerms.definition: The correlated part that averaging cannot remove.
The tree count, here 1000.

recall.question: Why is there almost no help at B = 1000?
recall.answer: The variance is 0.9 plus 0.1 over 1000 = 0.9001: the shared wobble dominates at any affordable B.

keyTerms.definition: Out-of-bag: points missed by a bootstrap replicate.
One bootstrap replicate, like rep 2.
The error resting here on points 0 and 1 only.

recall.question: Why is there no OOB prediction for point 2?
recall.answer: Rep 2 misses nothing, so point 2 loses its only OOB rep.

recall.question: What does the OOB error rest on?
recall.answer: Points 0 and 1 only.

keyTerms.definition: The AdaBoost vote weight 0.5 ln((1-eps)/eps).
The round error: 0.4 gives 0.2027, 0.1 gives 1.0986.

recall.question: Which round votes louder?
recall.answer: The accurate round: eps 0.1 gives alpha 1.0986 against 0.2027 for eps 0.4.

keyTerms.definition: The renormalized AdaBoost weights [1/6, 1/6, 1/6, 1/2].
The total 3/6 + 1/2 = 1, exact.

recall.question: Do the weights sum to 1?
recall.answer: Yes: 3/6 + 1/2 = 1, exact.

keyTerms.definition: The round-2 tree that contorts to fix the x = 3 point.
The heavy points the stump chases.
What to cap as a defense.

recall.question: What goes wrong in round 2?
recall.answer: The x = 3 point dominates the weights, so the stump contorts to fix it, likely at the price of a clean point.

recall.question: What is the defense?
recall.answer: Cap rounds, or switch to a loss that resists outliers.

keyTerms.definition: The [-1, 0, 1] whose sum is 0.
The start that guarantees the zero-sum residual vector.

recall.question: Why do the residuals sum to 0?
recall.answer: The mean start guarantees a zero-sum residual vector.

keyTerms.definition: The shrinkage 0.5 applied to the update.
The shrunken fit [1.5, 2.0, 2.25].

recall.question: What are the new residuals at nu = 0.5?

keyTerms.definition: The y - F that the boosting step fits.
The r = y - F for squared loss.

recall.question: What is the negative gradient for (1/2)(y - F)^2?
recall.answer: It is y - F = r.

keyTerms.definition: The metric that rewards the majority class either way.
The 95 negatives that all-negative predicts at 0.95.

recall.question: Why is accuracy misleading here?
recall.answer: Predicting positive always gets 0.05, worse than all-negative 0.95: accuracy rewards the majority class either way.

keyTerms.definition: TP over TP plus FP, here 0.4444.
TP over TP plus FN, here 0.8.

recall.question: What are precision, recall, and F1?
recall.answer: Precision is 0.4444, recall is 0.8, and F1 is 0.5714.

keyTerms.definition: The TPR-against-FPR plot that the huge TN count dilutes.
The curve with no such dilution.
FP over FP plus TN, here 0.0526 at 5 false positives.

recall.question: Why prefer the PR curve here?
recall.answer: With 95 negatives, even 5 false positives give FPR 0.0526 while precision is 4/9: the huge TN count dilutes the FPR axis, and the PR curve has no such dilution.

recall.question: What does ROC plot?
recall.answer: TPR against FPR = FP/(FP + TN).

keyTerms.definition: The 0.5 shared by the identical x1 and x2 splits.
The tie-break that picks x1 over x2.

recall.question: Why does the tree pick x1?
recall.answer: x2 equals x1 exactly, so the x2 split gives the same gain 0.5; the tree picks x1 by order, not merit.

keyTerms.definition: The credit that sums impurity gains per feature.
The pure-noise x1 credited 0.5.
The order rule that gives x1 the credit.

recall.question: How can gain importance mislead?
recall.answer: x1 is pure noise and x2 equals y exactly, yet listing x1 first with depth capped at 1 gives gain importance 0.5 to x1 and 0.0 to x2.

recall.question: Why does x1 get the credit?
recall.answer: The first split takes all the credit and order breaks the tie.

keyTerms.definition: The 0.58 from 0.7 squared plus 0.3 squared.
The computed expected accuracy.
What to report before claiming a win on tiny n.
The tiny sample where the gap could be luck.
The 0.83 clearing 0.5 on the same data.

recall.question: Why not claim a win at 0.83 versus 0.5?
recall.answer: n = 6 is tiny, so the gap could be luck; report a confidence interval or a larger test set first.

recall.question: What is the case for the win?
recall.answer: 0.83 clears 0.5 by a wide margin on the same data.

keyTerms.definition: The reference model a new model must beat.
The right baseline when one threshold separates the data.
The boundary needing depth, where a stump scores 0.5.

recall.question: When is the stump the right baseline?
recall.answer: When the data is linearly separable by one threshold; beating it is the minimum bar.

recall.question: When is it the wrong baseline?
recall.answer: When the true boundary needs depth, like XOR: then a stump scores 0.5 and every model beats it trivially.

keyTerms.definition: The predict function the assert checks.
The check that predictions equal [0,0,0,1,1,0].
The function splitting on x1 then x2 at 0.5.

recall.question: What does the assert check?
recall.answer: That predict on the six points gives [0,0,0,1,1,0].

recall.question: What is the split logic?
recall.answer: Return 0 if x1 is at most 0.5, else 1 if x2 is at most 0.5, else 1.

keyTerms.definition: The claim plus baseline, metric, and falsification condition.
The stated condition that would kill the claim.
The greedy depth-3 reference in the example.

recall.question: What form must a hypothesis take?
recall.answer: Claim, baseline, metric, and a falsification condition.

recall.question: What is the example falsification condition?
recall.answer: The claim is falsified if the gap is within noise over 20 seeds.

keyTerms.definition: The error rate of labeling by the node distribution.
The method minimizing exponential loss on reweighted points.
The method fitting the negative gradient of any differentiable loss.
TP over TP plus FP, paired with recall in the F1.

recall.question: What is the greedy limitation in L03?
recall.answer: It commits to the best single split without looking deeper; on XOR all single-split gains are 0.

recall.question: Why use the harmonic mean for F1?
recall.answer: It punishes a low value harder: the arithmetic mean would let high recall hide low precision.
